snippets.output: Yeast infections are primarily caused by the fungus Candida albicans.
Yeast infections are generally not considered highly contagious or transferable.
Yeast infections can be transmitted through sexual contact, but transmission through sexual contact is relatively uncommon.
Both men and women can develop symptoms after sexual intercourse with a partner who has a yeast infection.
A vaginal yeast infection can be passed from a mother to her baby during childbirth.
A vaginal yeast infection in a mother can lead to oral thrush in the infant.
Sharing personal items like towels or underwear can potentially spread yeast infections in rare cases.

Yeast infections can be transmitted under certain circumstances, including through sexual contact, and both men and women can develop symptoms after sexual intercourse with an infected partner. A mother with a vaginal yeast infection can also lead to oral thrush in the infant.
